chapter_title_ka: ქორწილი ავთანდილისა და თინათინისა არაბთა მეფისაგან
chapter_title_en: Marriage of Avtandil and Tinatin by the King of the Arabs
chapter_expert_explanation_en: King Rostevan and Tariel enthrone Avtandil beside Queen Tinatin and celebrate their royal wedding in Arabia, fulfilling the Prologue's and Georgian Encyclopedia's ideal of earthly love consummated in marriage and harmonious co-rule.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
მას დღე ავთანდილ ხელმწიფედ ზის და ხელმწიფე ზენია,
მასთანა მჯდომსა ტარიელს ჰშვენიან სინაზენია;
ნესტანჯარ ახლავს თინათინს, ვინ მჭვრეტთა ამაზრზენია,
და ჰგავს თუ, ცა მოდრკა ქვეყანად, შეყრილან ორნი მზენია.
stanzas.english_translation: That day Avt’handil sits as lord and is high king; tendernesses beautify Tariel who sits with him. Nestan-Djar, the amazer of onlookers, is with T’hinat’hin; it is as if heaven had bent down to earth, (and) two suns are united.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 61 ('Marriage of Avtandil and Tinatin by the King of the Arabs', Stanza 1549; Wardrop Stanza 1525): Part of the narrative sequence in which king Rostevan and Tariel enthrone Avtandil beside Queen Tinatin and celebrate their royal wedding in Arabia, fulfilling the Prologue's and Georgian Encyclopedia's ideal of earthly love consummated in marriage and harmonious co-rule.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
დაიწყეს მორთმა პურისა ლაშქართა მის მესავსისა,
ზროხა და ცხვარი დაკლული არს უმრავლესი ხავსისა,
შეიქმნა ძღვნობა ძღვენისა, მათისა შესამსგავსისა,
და მათ ყოვლთა შუქი ანათობს პირისა, მზისა მსგავსისა.
stanzas.english_translation: They began to bring bread to plenish the armies; beeves and sheep are slain more abundant than moss. There was made an offering of presents, fitting to them (i.e., to each after his rank) . The ray of the faces of them all lightens like the sun.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 61 ('Marriage of Avtandil and Tinatin by the King of the Arabs', Stanza 1550; Wardrop Stanza 1526): Part of the narrative sequence in which king Rostevan and Tariel enthrone Avtandil beside Queen Tinatin and celebrate their royal wedding in Arabia, fulfilling the Prologue's and Georgian Encyclopedia's ideal of earthly love consummated in marriage and harmonious co-rule.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
იაგუნდისა ჯამები იყვის, ლალისა ჭიქები,
კვლა უცხო ფერთა ჭურჭელთა სხდის უცხო-უცხო სიქები,
მის ქორწილისა მაქები კაცი ბრძენთაგან იქები,
და მჭვრეტელო, გულსა ეტყოდი: “ნუ აეხსნები, იქ ები!”
stanzas.english_translation: The bowls were of jacinth, the cups were of ruby; moreover, wondrously coloured vessels bear passing wondrous seals. The panegyrist of that wedding would be praised by the sages. O onlooker, thou wouldst have said unto thy heart: "Be not loosed, be bound there!"
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 61 ('Marriage of Avtandil and Tinatin by the King of the Arabs', Stanza 1551; Wardrop Stanza 1527): Part of the narrative sequence in which king Rostevan and Tariel enthrone Avtandil beside Queen Tinatin and celebrate their royal wedding in Arabia, fulfilling the Prologue's and Georgian Encyclopedia's ideal of earthly love consummated in marriage and harmonious co-rule.

stanzas.english_translation: The (female) minstrels approached from all sides, there was heard the sound of the cymbal; heaped lies a hillock of gold and cut rubies; for drinkers flows a fountain of wine from a hundred (runlets), like a canal; from twilight to dawn there was noise, the time of morning passed.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 61 ('Marriage of Avtandil and Tinatin by the King of the Arabs', Stanza 1552; Wardrop Stanza 1528): Part of the narrative sequence in which king Rostevan and Tariel enthrone Avtandil beside Queen Tinatin and celebrate their royal wedding in Arabia, fulfilling the Prologue's and Georgian Encyclopedia's ideal of earthly love consummated in marriage and harmonious co-rule.

stanzas.english_translation: None remained without a gift, neither lame nor crippled; pearls rolled to and fro, scattered, thrown about; satin and solid gold were of none account, to be carried away. For three days the King of the Indies was as a groomsman to Avt’handil.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 61 ('Marriage of Avtandil and Tinatin by the King of the Arabs', Stanza 1553; Wardrop Stanza 1529): Part of the narrative sequence in which king Rostevan and Tariel enthrone Avtandil beside Queen Tinatin and celebrate their royal wedding in Arabia, fulfilling the Prologue's and Georgian Encyclopedia's ideal of earthly love consummated in marriage and harmonious co-rule.

stanzas.english_translation: On the morrow the King of the Arabs again entertains; he is not listless. He said to Tariel: "Pleasant it is to gaze on thy sun (Nestan)! Thou art king of all kings, and she queen. It behoves us your footprints (dust of your feet), to pierce our ears for earrings (as slaves) (?).
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 61 ('Marriage of Avtandil and Tinatin by the King of the Arabs', Stanza 1554; Wardrop Stanza 1530): Part of the narrative sequence in which king Rostevan and Tariel enthrone Avtandil beside Queen Tinatin and celebrate their royal wedding in Arabia, fulfilling the Prologue's and Georgian Encyclopedia's ideal of earthly love consummated in marriage and harmonious co-rule.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“აწ, მეფეო, არ ეგების ჩვენი სხდომა თქვენად სწორად”.
სახელმწიფო საჯდომი და სხვა დაუდგა ტახტი შორად.
ქვემოდ დასხნა ავთანდილ და ცოლი მისი მათად სწორად.
და პირველ ძღვენი ტარიასთვის მოიღიან, იდვის გორად.
stanzas.english_translation: "Now, O king, it is not fitting that we should sit on a level with you!" The royal throne he (Rostevan) placed for (Tariel), and another couch apart; he placed Avt’handil and his wife lower down, according to their rank First of all they present gifts for Taria; they lie in a heap.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 61 ('Marriage of Avtandil and Tinatin by the King of the Arabs', Stanza 1555; Wardrop Stanza 1531): Part of the narrative sequence in which king Rostevan and Tariel enthrone Avtandil beside Queen Tinatin and celebrate their royal wedding in Arabia, fulfilling the Prologue's and Georgian Encyclopedia's ideal of earthly love consummated in marriage and harmonious co-rule.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
არაბთა მეფე მასპინძლობს, იქმს ოდენ არიფობასა,
ზოგჯერ მათ ახლავს, ზოგჯერ მათ, არ იხმობს ხელმწიფობასა,
გასცემს და უქებს ყოველნი უხვობა-იეფობასა,
და ფრიდონ ზის ახლოს ავთანდილს, ჩვეული ვით მეფობასა.
stanzas.english_translation: The King of the Arabs plays the host, he does nothing but entertain; sometimes he approaches these, sometimes those, he stands not upon his royal dignity; he gives, and all praise his ungrudging generosity. P’hridon sits near Avt’handil, as one accustomed to kingship.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 61 ('Marriage of Avtandil and Tinatin by the King of the Arabs', Stanza 1556; Wardrop Stanza 1532): Part of the narrative sequence in which king Rostevan and Tariel enthrone Avtandil beside Queen Tinatin and celebrate their royal wedding in Arabia, fulfilling the Prologue's and Georgian Encyclopedia's ideal of earthly love consummated in marriage and harmonious co-rule.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
მეფესა ქმრითურთ პატივი ჰქონდა ინდოთა ქალისა,
სიყვარული და ჩუქება, ვით სიძისა და სძალისა;
რომე სძღვნა, არა ეგების თქმა არცა ნაათალისა,
და თვითო სკიპტრა და პორფირი და გვირგვინები თვალისა.
stanzas.english_translation: The king (Rostevan) did honour to the daughter of the Indies and her husband, he gave them love and gifts, as to a son and daughter-in-law; it is impossible to tell even a tenth of what he gave, to each a sceptre, purple and jewelled crowns.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 61 ('Marriage of Avtandil and Tinatin by the King of the Arabs', Stanza 1557; Wardrop Stanza 1533): Part of the narrative sequence in which king Rostevan and Tariel enthrone Avtandil beside Queen Tinatin and celebrate their royal wedding in Arabia, fulfilling the Prologue's and Georgian Encyclopedia's ideal of earthly love consummated in marriage and harmonious co-rule.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
კვლა უძღვნა ძღვენი ორთავე, მსგავსი მათისა ბედისა,
ათასი თვალი, ნაშობი რომანულისა დედისა,
კვლა მარგალიტი ათასი, მართ ვითა კვერცხი ტრედისა,
და ათასი ცხენი ტაიჭი, სიდიდით მსგავსი ქედისა.
stanzas.english_translation: Still he gave to both gifts fitting their fate; a thousand gems born of a Roman hen; then a thousand pearls like a dove's egg; a thousand steeds, in size each like a hill:
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 61 ('Marriage of Avtandil and Tinatin by the King of the Arabs', Stanza 1558; Wardrop Stanza 1534): Part of the narrative sequence in which king Rostevan and Tariel enthrone Avtandil beside Queen Tinatin and celebrate their royal wedding in Arabia, fulfilling the Prologue's and Georgian Encyclopedia's ideal of earthly love consummated in marriage and harmonious co-rule.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
ფრიდონს უძღვნა ცხრა ტაბაკი მარგალიტი თავ-შედგმული,
ცხრა ტაიჭი, ძვირფასისა უნაგრითა შეკაზმული.
ინდოთ მეფე თაყვანსა სცემს ლაღი, ბრძენი, არ-მახმული,
და მადლი ჰკადრა ფხიზელურად, თუცა იყო ღვინო-სმული.
stanzas.english_translation: To P’hridon he gave nines trays full to the brim with pearls, nine steeds richly saddled. The King of the Indians does homage with dignity; wise, not drunkenly; he gave thanks soberly though he had drunk of the wine.'
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 61 ('Marriage of Avtandil and Tinatin by the King of the Arabs', Stanza 1559; Wardrop Stanza 1535): Part of the narrative sequence in which king Rostevan and Tariel enthrone Avtandil beside Queen Tinatin and celebrate their royal wedding in Arabia, fulfilling the Prologue's and Georgian Encyclopedia's ideal of earthly love consummated in marriage and harmonious co-rule.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
რას ვაგრძელებდე, გარდახდეს დღენი ერთისა თვისანი.
თამაშობდიან, არ იყვნეს ყოლა გაყრანი სმისანი.
ტარიელს სძღვნიან უცხონი თვალნი ლალისა ქვისანი,
და მათ ყოვლთა მათნი ელვანი ჰფარვენ მართ ვითა მზისანი.
stanzas.english_translation: Why should I lengthen (speech)? The days of one month passed. They sported, they ceased not at all from drinking. To Tariel they presented wondrous jewels of ruby stone. Their radiance like the sun's covers them all.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 61 ('Marriage of Avtandil and Tinatin by the King of the Arabs', Stanza 1560; Wardrop Stanza 1536): Part of the narrative sequence in which king Rostevan and Tariel enthrone Avtandil beside Queen Tinatin and celebrate their royal wedding in Arabia, fulfilling the Prologue's and Georgian Encyclopedia's ideal of earthly love consummated in marriage and harmonious co-rule.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
ტარიელ ჰგვანდის ვარდსა და იყვის ფიფქისა მთოველად,
ავთანდილ როსტანს წინაშე გაგზავნა დასათხოველად;
შესთვალა: “შენი სიახლე კმა ჩემად ლხინად ყოველად,
და მტერთა აქვს ჩემი სამეფო, ვიცი მუნ შიგან მძოველად”.
stanzas.english_translation: Tariel was like a rose, and was snowing a light snow shower; he sent Avt’handil to Rosten to ask for leave; he gave him this message: "To be near thee is enough for me as full joy, (but) enemies hold my kingdom, I know they are eating up the land.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 61 ('Marriage of Avtandil and Tinatin by the King of the Arabs', Stanza 1561; Wardrop Stanza 1537): Part of the narrative sequence in which king Rostevan and Tariel enthrone Avtandil beside Queen Tinatin and celebrate their royal wedding in Arabia, fulfilling the Prologue's and Georgian Encyclopedia's ideal of earthly love consummated in marriage and harmonious co-rule.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“უცებნი მოსრნის მცოდნელთა ცოდნამან, ხელოვნებამან.
ვეჭვ, მოქცეს თქვენცა დაღრეჯა ჩემმან რასაცა ვნებამან;
წავიდე, ავი არ მიყოს მე აქა დაყოვნებამან,
და ადრე კვლა გნახნე მორჭმულნი, ინებოს ღმრთისა ნებამან”.
stanzas.english_translation: "The knowledge and art of the learned destroy the unlearned. I think any hurt to me would bring somewhat of sadness into you too. I go that tarrying here may not bring evil upon me, soon again may I see you happy, may God's will grant it!"
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 61 ('Marriage of Avtandil and Tinatin by the King of the Arabs', Stanza 1562; Wardrop Stanza 1538): Part of the narrative sequence in which king Rostevan and Tariel enthrone Avtandil beside Queen Tinatin and celebrate their royal wedding in Arabia, fulfilling the Prologue's and Georgian Encyclopedia's ideal of earthly love consummated in marriage and harmonious co-rule.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
როსტევან ჰკადრა: “მეფეო, რად ხართ რასაცა რიდითა,
რაცა გიჯობდეს, იქმოდით, გასჭვრეტდით, გაიცდიდითა,
ავთანდილ თანა წამოგყვეს,წადით ლაშქრითა დიდითა.
და თქვენთა მტერთა და ორგულთა დაჰფრეწდით, დაცასჭრიდითა“.
stanzas.english_translation: Rostevan said: "O king, why art thou so bashful? Whatever is best for you do it, look into it, examine it. [paragraph continues] Avt’handil will accompany thee, go with a great host; rend in pieces and cut up your enemies and them that are traitors."
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 61 ('Marriage of Avtandil and Tinatin by the King of the Arabs', Stanza 1563; Wardrop Stanza 1539): Part of the narrative sequence in which king Rostevan and Tariel enthrone Avtandil beside Queen Tinatin and celebrate their royal wedding in Arabia, fulfilling the Prologue's and Georgian Encyclopedia's ideal of earthly love consummated in marriage and harmonious co-rule.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
ავთანდილ უთხრა ტარიელს ესე სიტყვები ორები.
მან უთხრა: “აგრე ნუ უბნობ, შეცევ ბროლისა ყორები,
ახლად შეყრილსა მთვარესა, მზეო, ვით მოეშორები?”
და ავთანდილ უთხრა: “მაგითა შენგან არ მოვიღორები”.
stanzas.english_translation: Avt’handil said to Tariel those (same) two words (that Rostevan had said). He (Tariel) said: "Speak not thus; guard the crystal mounds. How canst thou, O sun, depart from the newly united moon!" Avt’handil said: "I shall not be seduced by thee with this:
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 61 ('Marriage of Avtandil and Tinatin by the King of the Arabs', Stanza 1564; Wardrop Stanza 1540): Part of the narrative sequence in which king Rostevan and Tariel enthrone Avtandil beside Queen Tinatin and celebrate their royal wedding in Arabia, fulfilling the Prologue's and Georgian Encyclopedia's ideal of earthly love consummated in marriage and harmonious co-rule.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“არ დია გინდა დამაგდო, წახვიდე ჩემად მზრახავად!
«ცოლი უყვარსო, გამწირა» იყო ამისად მსახავად;
მე დავრჩე შენი გაყრილი თავისა მევაგლახავად?
და კაცსა მოყვრისა გაწირვა, ახ, მოუხდების, ახ ავად!”
stanzas.english_translation: "Of a truth thou wishest not to forsake me while thou goest away slandering me, saying: 'He loveth his wife, forsooth; he hath forsaken me, ’twas like him!' Am I to remain sundered from thee and an object of pity to myself! For a man to forsake his friend! . . . Ugh! Ugh! he will do ill!"
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 61 ('Marriage of Avtandil and Tinatin by the King of the Arabs', Stanza 1565; Wardrop Stanza 1541): Part of the narrative sequence in which king Rostevan and Tariel enthrone Avtandil beside Queen Tinatin and celebrate their royal wedding in Arabia, fulfilling the Prologue's and Georgian Encyclopedia's ideal of earthly love consummated in marriage and harmonious co-rule.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
ტარიელს უგავს სიცილი ბროლისა ვარდთათ ფრქვევასა,
უბრძანა: “ვიტყვი უშენოდ შენისა უფრო მე ვასა;
რათგან გწადიან, წამომყევ, დამწამებ ნურას თნევასა”.
და ავთანდილ ბრძანებს ლაშქართა ყოვლგნით მისთანა წვევსა.
stanzas.english_translation: Tariel's smile is like the sprinkling of crystal with roses. He said: "Absent from thee I bewail myself more than thou. Since thou wishest it, come away with me, accuse me not of flattery." Avt’handil commands troops to be summoned to him from all sides.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 61 ('Marriage of Avtandil and Tinatin by the King of the Arabs', Stanza 1566; Wardrop Stanza 1542): Part of the narrative sequence in which king Rostevan and Tariel enthrone Avtandil beside Queen Tinatin and celebrate their royal wedding in Arabia, fulfilling the Prologue's and Georgian Encyclopedia's ideal of earthly love consummated in marriage and harmonious co-rule.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
შეყარნა სპანი არაბეთს, აღარა ხანსა ზმულია;
კაცი ოთხმოცი ათასი, ყველაი დაკაზმულია.

და არაბთა მეფე მათითა გაყრითა ნაღველ-ჭმულია.
stanzas.english_translation: He assembled the armies of Arabia, no time is wasted; eighty thousand men were all arrayed, man and horse clad in armour of Khvarazmia. The King of the Arabs eats the gall of bitterness at their separation.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 61 ('Marriage of Avtandil and Tinatin by the King of the Arabs', Stanza 1567; Wardrop Stanza 1543): Part of the narrative sequence in which king Rostevan and Tariel enthrone Avtandil beside Queen Tinatin and celebrate their royal wedding in Arabia, fulfilling the Prologue's and Georgian Encyclopedia's ideal of earthly love consummated in marriage and harmonious co-rule.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
ერთმანერთისა გაყრილნი ქალნი ორნივე, დობილნი,
ერთმანერთისა დად-ფიცნი, სიტყვისა გამონდობილნი,

stanzas.english_translation: Parting each from other, both maidens, the adopted sisters, sworn with the oath of sisterhood, trusting in each other's word, with breast welded to breast, with neck riveted to neck, wept. The onlookers, too, had their hearts consumed.

stanzas.english_translation: When the moon is on a level with the star of dawn, both shine equally; should (one) go away, (the other also) is removed; if it go not away, the sky will make it remove; to look at them the onlooker must become a hill and a mountain (?).
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 61 ('Marriage of Avtandil and Tinatin by the King of the Arabs', Stanza 1569; Wardrop Stanza 1545): Part of the narrative sequence in which king Rostevan and Tariel enthrone Avtandil beside Queen Tinatin and celebrate their royal wedding in Arabia, fulfilling the Prologue's and Georgian Encyclopedia's ideal of earthly love consummated in marriage and harmonious co-rule.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:

იგივე გაჰყრის, სიშორე არა თუ ნებით სწადიან,
ვარდსა სწებენ და აპობენ, ტირან და ცრემლნი ჩადიან.
და მათთა გამყრელთა ყოველთა სიცოცხლე არ იქადიან.
stanzas.english_translation: He who created them such, He Himself shall sunder them, though of their own will they desire not parting. They glue together and cleave the rose, they weep and tears flow; all those who parted from them thought their lives of no account.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 61 ('Marriage of Avtandil and Tinatin by the King of the Arabs', Stanza 1570; Wardrop Stanza 1546): Part of the narrative sequence in which king Rostevan and Tariel enthrone Avtandil beside Queen Tinatin and celebrate their royal wedding in Arabia, fulfilling the Prologue's and Georgian Encyclopedia's ideal of earthly love consummated in marriage and harmonious co-rule.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
ნესტან-დარეჯან თქვა: “ნეტამც ყოლა არ შემოგცნებოდი,
მზისა გამყრელი გაყრითა აწ ასრე არ დავდნებოდი.
ამბავსა სცნევდი, მაცნევდი, წიგნითა მეუბნებოდი,
და ვითა მე შენთვის დამწვარვარ, აგრე შენ ჩემთვის ჰბნდებოდი”.
stanzas.english_translation: Nestan-Daredjan said: "Would that I had never come to know thee! Separated from the sun I should not now be thus melted by parting. Thou shalt know tidings of me; let me have news of thee, speak to me in letters. As I am burned up for thy sake, thou shalt melt for mine."
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 61 ('Marriage of Avtandil and Tinatin by the King of the Arabs', Stanza 1571; Wardrop Stanza 1547): Part of the narrative sequence in which king Rostevan and Tariel enthrone Avtandil beside Queen Tinatin and celebrate their royal wedding in Arabia, fulfilling the Prologue's and Georgian Encyclopedia's ideal of earthly love consummated in marriage and harmonious co-rule.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:

რადმცა გაგწირე, თუ ვითა გაყრასა მოვითმინებო!
ღმრთისაგან დღეთა თხოვისა ნაცვლად სიკვდილი ვინებო,
და აგრემცა მივი, რაზომსა მე ცრემლსა დავიდინებო!”
stanzas.english_translation: T’hinat’hin said: "O sun, delight of them that gaze on thee! How can I give thee up, or how can I endure parting! Instead of praying for days from God, I shall desire death. Mayst thou have as many days as I shall shed tears!"
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 61 ('Marriage of Avtandil and Tinatin by the King of the Arabs', Stanza 1572; Wardrop Stanza 1548): Part of the narrative sequence in which king Rostevan and Tariel enthrone Avtandil beside Queen Tinatin and celebrate their royal wedding in Arabia, fulfilling the Prologue's and Georgian Encyclopedia's ideal of earthly love consummated in marriage and harmonious co-rule.

ქვე დამდგომმან წამავალსა ვერ მოსწყვიდნა ყოლა თვალნი.

stanzas.english_translation: Again they kissed each other, those ladies parted; she who was left there could not take her eyes away from her who was gone; she too looks back, therefore flames consumed her. I cannot write down a tenth part of that I could wish!

stanzas.english_translation: Rostan at their departure was made more mad than madmen; a thousand times he says, "Woe is me!" not merely once doth he sigh; hot flows the spring of tears, as if a cauldron were being heated. Tariel's face is drawn, the soft snow falls gently, it wastes away.

stanzas.english_translation: The king crushed Tariel's rose with embracing and kissing. Quoth he: "Your presence hitherto seems like a dream to me; when thou art gone afar from me I shall remain with my sufferings twentyfold increased. Life was given to us by thee; by thee also shall we be slain."

სრულად ლაშქართა სდიოდა ცრემლი, მინდორთა სალამე:

stanzas.english_translation: Tariel mounted and parting from the king gave him a farewell greeting; all the soldiers shed tears moistening the meadows, they said: "The sun hastes to greet thee, haste thou too to meet him." He said: "Weeping for your sake, why should I hasten?"

stanzas.english_translation: They set out and departed with many troops and much baggage--Tariel, P’hridon, Avt’handil, (all) well provided; he had eighty thousand men with worthy steeds; the three went on, helpful one to another.

stanzas.english_translation: The three went their way--God can never create their like again! They were met; none dared withstand them. In the plain they tarried for dinner when morning was past. As was fitting they feasted; they drank wine, not buttermilk.
